title: Build a cladogram from a trait table

stimulus.title: Characters of five fish species
stimulus.text: Researchers studied four closely related fish species from a lake system, P, Q, R and S, and a species from a nearby river, O, which other evidence shows lies outside the group formed by the four lake species. They scored five characters as present (1) or absent (0).

table.caption: Characters of species O, P, Q, R and S (1 = present, 0 = absent)
cols: First and second back fins joined

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify the outgroup, and describe how it is used to decide which state of each character is derived.

rubric.point: Identifies species O as the outgroup AND describes that a state found in the outgroup (here, 0 for every character) is taken to be ancestral, so the state found only within the lake species (1) is derived.
accept: O; characters O has are ancestral, so the present (1) states are derived
O, because it lies outside the group; states shared with O are the older states
the outgroup O shows the ancestral condition (absent), so presence is the derived condition

parts.sample: Species O is the outgroup. Because O lies outside the group of lake species, the states it has are taken as the ancestral ones. O has none of the five characters, so absence (0) is ancestral for each, and presence (1) in some lake species is derived.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Construct a cladogram of the five species that is consistent with the data. Mark where each of the five characters arose. You may draw it or write it with nested parentheses and list where each character arose.

rubric.point: Shows the branching order O, then P, then Q, with R and S as sister taxa, written (O, (P, (Q, (R, S)))) or drawn equivalently, AND places dark bars on the branch to P, Q, R and S; enlarged jaw on the branch to Q, R and S; joined fins on the branch to R and S; no pelvic fins on the branch to S; blue throat on the branch to R.
accept: (O,(P,(Q,(R,S)))) with bars before P, jaw before Q, joined fins before R+S, pelvic loss on S, blue throat on R
a drawn cladogram with the same nesting and the five characters on the correct branches
nesting O | P | Q | (R, S), each character marked once on the stem of the group that has it

parts.sample: (O, (P, (Q, (R, S)))). Dark bars arose on the branch leading to P, Q, R and S; the enlarged lower jaw on the branch leading to Q, R and S; joined back fins on the branch leading to R and S; loss of pelvic fins on the branch to S alone; the blue throat on the branch to R alone. Each character arises once, so the tree needs 5 changes.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: For the clade made up of R and S, identify one shared derived character and one shared ancestral character, and explain the difference between them.

rubric.point: Identifies joined back fins as the shared derived character of the R-S clade AND dark bars or the enlarged jaw as a shared ancestral character within it, explaining that the derived character arose in the most recent common ancestor of R and S alone, while the ancestral one was inherited from an older ancestor and is also found outside the clade (in Q or P), so it cannot set R and S apart.
accept: derived: joined fins, arose in the R-S ancestor; ancestral: enlarged jaw, also in Q, inherited from an older ancestor
joined fins unite R and S only; dark bars are shared by P and Q too, so for this clade they are ancestral
shared derived = new in the clade's ancestor (joined fins); shared ancestral = from an earlier ancestor (bars or jaw)

parts.sample: Joined back fins are a shared derived character of the R-S clade: they arose in the most recent common ancestor of R and S and are found in no other species in the table. The enlarged lower jaw is a shared ancestral character within this clade: R and S both have it, but so does Q, because it arose in an older ancestor of Q, R and S. A shared ancestral character cannot show that R and S are each other's closest relatives; only a shared derived one can.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: New DNA sequence data show that Q and R share many mutations that S lacks, so Q and R are sister taxa, with S joining them next. Predict how the cladogram changes, and explain what the new tree implies about the history of the joined back fins.

rubric.point: Predicts the new tree (O, (P, (S, (Q, R)))) AND explains that joined back fins, found in R and S but not Q, must then have arisen twice independently (in S and in R, convergent evolution) or arisen once in the ancestor of S, Q and R and been lost in Q: either way, two changes instead of one.
accept: (O,(P,(S,(Q,R)))); the joined fins evolved twice, once in S and once in R, or were lost in Q
S now branches before Q and R; the fin character needs an extra change, either convergence or a loss in Q
new tree puts Q with R; joined fins are no longer a single shared derived character, so they arose independently or reverted in Q

parts.sample: The new cladogram is (O, (P, (S, (Q, R)))): S branches off before Q and R, which are sister taxa. Joined back fins are found in S and R but not in Q, so they can no longer be explained by one change. Either they arose twice independently, once in the S line and once in the R line (convergent evolution), or they arose once in the ancestor of S, Q and R and were later lost in Q. Both need two changes, which is why a tree is a hypothesis that new evidence can revise.
